correctness.rationale: For each positive ring size, Rule 90 has kernel equal to period-two binary configurations: dimension one for odd sizes and dimension two for even sizes. Its image is exactly the corresponding parity-constraint subspace. A rotation-stabilizer Burnside count of each labeled fiber reduces the number of input-necklace predecessors to a totient-weighted divisor sum. Evaluating odd, even and four-divisible divisors gives the five-case classification, including n=1,2 and periodic input words. The extracted verifier exhaustively independently checked 8,923 output necklaces through n=16 and five length-eight witnesses. The general proof, not the finite enumeration, proves the quantified theorem.

originality.rationale: The closest literature explicitly separates uniform labeled Rule 90 preimage counts, all-rule finite necklace-network visualization, and the adjacent-XOR necklace map. The claimed primitive-period and primitive-block parity classification of all individual quotient in-degrees is not a stated or immediately implied result of the inspected source passages. The adjacent-XOR square equivalence is acknowledged and remains a substantive historical-priority risk; unpublished/unindexed coverage cannot be ruled out.
residual_risks: Historical formulations of inverse degrees for the square of the Ducci/adjacent-XOR map might imply the same classification, and unindexed literature was not exhaustively accessible.
Some large foundational PDFs were read through relevant extracted sections rather than fully from cover to cover; no universal negative novelty assertion rests solely on them.
Published finite necklace figures might enable readers to deduce small cases but cannot establish all lengths without additional proof.

value.rationale: The 2024 elementary-CA necklace-network setting naturally asks for incoming-edge multiplicities, which can govern inverse search and quotient graph branching. Here a complete nonconstant 0-to-4 local-degree classification valid for all positive ring lengths is determined from intrinsic primitive-period parity statistics. It exposes exact ways rotation collapses the uniform 2/4 labeled fibers. This is not a selected finite case, routine parameter substitution, or arbitrary invariant; the result gives a natural complete inverse-branching theorem.
